Section 4. Consequences of Positive Tests. When a university receives notice of an employee’s positive test, the university will take one or more of the following actions in addition to removing the employee from safety-sensitive functions:

(A) If the test is a Random, Reasonable Suspicion, and/or a Pre-employment Test

(1) Temporarily assign the employee to non-safety-sensitive functions;

(2) Allow an employee to take accrued leave, or leave without pay, pursuant to the requirements of the Agreement if the university does not assign non-safety-sensitive functions;

(3) Refer the employee to rehabilitation and last chance agreement;

(4) Take disciplinary action pursuant to the requirements of the Agreement.

In the case of pre-employment testing for promotions, demotions, or transfers where the employee is moving from a position that does not require a CDL to a position that requires a CDL, an additional option is to rescind the appointment.

(B) If the test is a Post-Accident, Follow-up, and/or Return-to-Duty Test

(1) Refer employee to rehabilitation and last chance agreement; and/or

(2) Take disciplinary action pursuant to the requirement of the Agreement.

This Agreement does not waive employee rights under CFR Part 382.505 as it applies to alcohol test results of 0.02 to 0.039.

The parties acknowledge that the university, at its own discretion, may decide to offer a last chance agreement to an employee as an alternative to termination. However, nothing in this Article shall preclude the university from issuing a lesser form of discipline in conjunction with offering a last chance agreement.
